newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone sells majority stake in oil company.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone sells majority stake in oil company.

text.p: Sierra Leone's government has sold its majority holding in National Petroleum (NP), once owned completely by the impoverished West African state, Finance Ministry officials said on Friday.
Brimah Conteh, technical coordinator of the government's privatisation programme said 55 percent of NP's shares had been transferred to LEONCO, a private company.
The government had a 60 percent stake in NP, while privately-owned Precious Minerals Marketing Company held 40 percent. The remaining five percent government stake will be sold to NP employees.
LEONCO, was set up to bid for the government's shares and has paid an initial $1.55 million, to be followed by the same amount in 12 monthly instalments.

Sierra Leone, ruined by war, is utterly aid dependent and on Thursday said the International Monetary Fund had promised a $14 million loan because it is satisfied with economic policies which include privatisation and spending controls.
